title: Introduce observability stability bridge and log vet for low-latency paths
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Background: Our runtime has accumulated lightweight but performance-sensitive observability hooks injected in several hot paths (gpu tokenizers, KV cache hot-get, and batching coordinator). Recent profiling shows intermittent p99 latency spikes caused by synchronized flushes in the logging layer and occasional blocking in the tracing span builder when sampling logic consults multiple external providers. These issues are increasing tail latency on small requests (<= 32 tokens) and complicating SLO guarantees for hosted tiers.

Problem statement: We need a minimal compatibility layer that stabilizes observability behavior on low-latency code paths without requiring a full rewrite of OTEL instrumentation across services. Aim to remove synchronous flushes and reduce hot-path allocations while preserving trace fidelity and sampling semantics for upstream analysis.

Goals: 
- Introduce an "observability stability bridge" (a thin in-process proxy) that:
  - answers sampling decisions with a fast cached policy (<= 200ns check)
  - routes traces and logs to buffered background writers on critical low-latency paths
  - exposes a no-op fastpath when tracing is disabled for a tenant
- Harden log path by adding a "log vet" step that de-duplicates high-cardinality log fields and enforces size bounds before any formatted allocation occurs
- Remove synchronous span flushes from hot code paths and replace with async handoff and bounded ring buffer to avoid CPU stalls
- Maintain compatibility with existing ingestion/export layers (OpenTelemetry collector, existing forwarding shims) so downstream analytics remain unchanged

Proposed approach: 
1) Implement a small in-memory policy cache (LRU with TTL) used by the sampling API. Cache hits must be lock-free for readers (atomic pointer swap pattern) and updated by a periodic background reconciler.
2) Add a lightweight SpanBuilder facade used in hot paths that constructs only essential metadata; full attribute enrichment deferred to a background worker that can attach heavy attributes after span creation.
3) Replace direct io/flush calls in the runtime logger with a LogVet pipeline stage that: (a) validates size and cardinality, (b) drops or masks ephemeral high-card fields per configurable rules, (c) enqueues sanitized log frames into a bounded buffer drained by background flushers.
4) Provide a feature flag + per-tenant opt-out to toggle strict vetting during rollout.
5) Add e2e perf test suite that runs microbenchmarks for small request tails and measures allocations, syscall counts, and p99 latency.

Acceptance criteria: 
- p99 latency for <32-token requests improves by at least 15% in canary compared to baseline under a 1000 qps test with realistic prefix caching.
- Tracing sampling decision latency under 95th percentile < 500ns for cache hits.
- No loss of exported spans when running with standard collector configuration (validated by integration test).
- Rollout can be gated per-tenant and toggled without restarts.

Rollout plan: 
- Week 1: implement policy cache + SpanBuilder facade behind feature flag; unit tests and microbenchmarks.
- Week 2: implement LogVet stage and bounded flushers; integrate into runtime agent; run internal perf harness.
- Week 3: canary deployment to 2 low-traffic hosts + telemetry comparison; iterate on thresholds.
- Week 4: widen to 10% traffic with tenant flag; monitor errors, export completeness, and latency.
- Week 5: full production rollout if metrics pass.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: deferred enrichment could cause missing attributes in traces consumed by downstream alerts. Mitigation: ensure background enrichment attaches attributes before export deadline; for critical attributes, keep sync path.
- Risk: aggressive vetting masks fields that debugging relies on. Mitigation: make vet rules configurable and reversible per-tenant; log masked-field counts to a diagnostics stream.

Links & artifacts: 
- Prototype microbench: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability-proto/pull/37 (PR will be created)
- Design notes (internal Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/obs-stability-bridge
- Perf harness dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/obs/microbench-stability-bridge
comments: 2025-01-20 - Ethan Park: Spike complete for policy cache reading pattern. Lock-free reader using atomic.Pointer reduced sampling check median from 1.1us to 160ns in the microbench. Submitting spike notes to the design doc.
2025-01-28 - Asha Kapoor: Reviewed spike; asked to verify cross-language semantics for Python runtime. Filed ENG-842712 to track Python binding compatibility (dependency).

2025-02-05 - Ethan Park: Implemented SpanBuilder facade and basic LogVet interface. Added feature flag observability.stability_bridge on the runtime. Unit tests added; microbench shows allocation reduction ~40% on hot paths.

2025-02-14 - Marina Gomez (SRE): Canary template prepared; suggested default buffer size increase to 32k to avoid drops under bursty loads. Also called out the need for a diagnostic metric for masked fields.

2025-02-25 - Ethan Park: Integrated bounded ring buffer drainers and added mask-count metric. Running canary on two hosts; preliminary p99 delta ~12% improvement. Will iterate on vet rules to reach acceptance target.
